clusters.text: The Democrats have swept to victory in the US midterm elections, taking control of Congress. While the incumbent president's party generally tends to have a bad night in these elections, the scale of the Republican defeat is being viewed as a resounding rejection of Donald Trump's two years in the White House. From angry voters to an unpopular president , here are five reasons why the Republicans lost so many seats . From coast to coast, voters across the US have been grappling with the soaring cost of essentials. That anger was palpable on the ground in key races. "Gas prices, grocery prices, everything's going up," one North Carolina voter told the BBC ahead of the elections, adding that she had switched her vote from Republican to Democratic this election. Prices increased by 3.7% in the year to September, driven higher by fuel and energy prices. Average US retail diesel prices in early October were just shy of the record of $6.52 (£4.83) per gallon seen in September, according to government data. Almost eight in 10 voters (79%) said inflation had caused them and their family a severe or moderate hardship in the past year, according to data from voter polls. And more than six in 10 respondents laid the blame for that at the feet of Trump, saying they thought higher than usual prices were because of the president's policies. Fuel prices then shot up after Tehran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz in retaliation, strangling a key artery for the passage of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG). US voters have been paying the price at the petrol pump ever since. The war has proved broadly unpopular with most Americans. clusters.text: Vice-President JD Vance sent shockwaves through Washington on Wednesday by blaming his party's midterm defeat squarely on the Iran war, in what was widely interpreted as an effort to distance himself from President Donald Trump ahead of a potential 2028 White House run. In a carefully calibrated, 600-word statement on X, the vice-president acknowledged that Trump's 2024 voters had deserted Republicans in the midterm election . "The reason we lost is the war," he wrote. "The president himself said so last night." In interviews late Tuesday night and Wednesday, Trump had defended the war but acknowledged that it played a factor in Democrats flipping control of the US House of Representatives and the Senate . Vance's view on the war in Iran is an open secret in Washington. While he has repeatedly backed the conflict since the US and Israel attacked Tehran in February, he has reportedly expressed opposition in private meetings with administration officials. But those disagreements had been kept out of the public eye - until now. Hours after Trump and the party were handed a bruising election defeat, Vance made clear that he felt the decision to go to war was a clear political mistake. "If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that's at least honest," Vance said. It was a striking statement, and one with no recent precedent: it's hard to recall a similar moment in recent US political history when a sitting vice-president has so sharply broken with the president on a signature foreign policy issue. Then came an arguably even greater surprise: Trump - who typically demands steadfast loyalty from his senior advisers - agreed with Vance that the midterms were "largely" decided by the war. He added that he would "do it again" if given the same choices. But the mingling of time periods also extends to the development team. While Ocarina’s remake was led by producers Eiji Aonuma (a director on the original game who is now the franchise’s steward at Nintendo) and Hidemaro Fujibayashi (best known for directing Breath of the Wild and its sequel), the team also featured a number of younger developers, including some who had never played the original. According to Fujibayashi, those new voices provided some much-needed perspective that shaped the remake. “What really impressed me was the fact that they really embraced the theme of what not to change from the original,” Fujibayashi tells me ahead of Ocarina of Time’s launch when explaining the influence of the younger team members, who approached the project “very carefully.” He adds that “I feel confident that they weren’t necessarily pursuing something new for the sake of novelty when it might be unneeded and clutter the experience. And I think that’s a perspective they’ll be able to bring to future projects as well.” Much has changed since Ocarina of Time first debuted on the Nintendo 64 in 1998, and Aonuma has had the unique perspective of working on both iterations of the game. clusters.text: Between 10,000 and 13,000 grizzly bears are estimated to live in British Columbia (file image) A mother and daughter have died after a suspected grizzly bear attack in the Canadian province of British Columbia, their family has announced. The women - identified as Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter Selah Reed, 20 -were reported missing on 1 November when they did not return from what was supposed to be a short afternoon walk, the family said. Their remains were found in a trail area in Bella Coola, according to the BC Conservation Officer Service (BCCOS), which said evidence at the scene "suggested an animal may have been involved". Conservation officers are working to track down any bears involved. Balcarras' remains were found on Monday and Reed's on Tuesday during search efforts by conservation officers and the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP). Jeff Tyre, an inspector with the BCCOS, said it was not yet clear if more than one was potentially involved in the women's deaths. He added that any captured bear would be assessed and if it is found to have been involved in the attack "it will be dispatched in accordance with provincial human-wildlife conflict response guidelines to protect public safety". Balcarras and Reed were "two peas in a pod" who "got along really, really well" and shared many hobbies, Balcarras' brother, Josh Balcarras, told CBC. "When Jenny hiked, Selah was right there beside her," he said. Balcarras had recently moved to Bella Coola to pursue a new career and begin a new chapter in her life, according to an online fundraiser to help the family with funeral costs. Grizzly bears are listed as a species of "special concern" under federal legislation, and are an important part of the British Columbia landscape, according to Environmental Reporting BC , external . Between 10,000 and 13,000 grizzly bears are estimated to live in the province, according to the province's Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks, which has classified them as vulnerable. According to the ministry, conflicts between bears and humans are "relatively rare" unless the animals are startled or protecting their cubs and food. But there have been a number of attacks in British Columbia in recent years. A grizzly bear injured two hikers in the McGregor Mountain area in October 2025, one of whom died later due to critical injuries. The bear was later found dead.

clusters.title: Ranchi Railway Stations Tighten Security for Festive Rush
clusters.text: Ranchi and Hatia railway stations have intensified security and passenger-management arrangements ahead of the expected Diwali and Chhath Puja rush, with holding areas, barricades, CCTV surveillance and additional Railway Protection Force personnel being deployed to manage crowds and reduce the risk of dangerous congestion. At Ranchi station, two passenger holding areas, each with a capacity of about 250 people, are being established to regulate inflow during peak periods. Barricades have already been installed across the station premises and platforms, while additional RPF personnel have been positioned at platforms, entry and exit points and ticket counters. The measures are intended to control queues, regulate passenger movement and support orderly boarding. RPF personnel will implement one-by-one boarding on platforms and ensure that trains leave only after passengers have boarded safely, according to Sishupal Kumar, the RPF inspector in-charge at Ranchi station. “After successfully managing the Durga Puja rush at the station without any untoward incident, we have now tightened our arrangements for Diwali and Chhath Puja rush by deploying a sufficient number of RPF personnel,” Kumar told the Times of India. The station is being monitored around the clock through CCTV cameras, Kumar said. Separate emergency exits have also been designated in addition to the main entry and exit points for use during an emergency. Similar crowd-control arrangements have been made at Hatia station, where barricade tapes have been installed on platforms. Passengers have been cautioned against crossing the railway line before designated trains arrive. Rupesh Kumar, in-charge of the Hatia railway police station, said the passenger rush at Hatia was lower than at Ranchi station. The railway has also scheduled special services to accommodate increased festive-season demand.
